cohort_total_n_excerpt: Of 35,242 men who completed the baseline dietary and supplemental questionnaire, 832 men developed invasive prostate cancers between October 2000 and December 2004.
reason: The prospective cohort abstract reports both overall incident invasive prostate cancer and incident advanced prostate cancer defined as regionally invasive or distant metastatic disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Ten-year average intake of supplemental zinc was not associated with a reduced prostate cancer risk overall (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) = 0.82 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.58-1.14) for >15 mg/day vs. nonuse, P for trend = 0.44);
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate is explicitly for overall prostate cancer risk, rather than advanced prostate cancer.

additional_estimates.comparison: 10-yr average supplemental zinc intake >15 mg/day versus nonuse
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: however, risk of advanced prostate cancer (regionally invasive or distant metastatic, n = 123) decreased with greater intake of supplemental zinc (adjusted HR = 0.34, 95% CI = 0.13-1.09 for 10-yr average intake > 15 mg/day vs. nonuse, P for trend = 0.04).
